Priya (CS): Heads up — Brightline reported a spike in p99 text-gen latency after last night’s rollout, ~5–10% above SLA for some routes. CS is asking for an engineering ETA on mitigation. Logs attached in Zendesk 4521.
Samir (eng-oncall): Ack. Can you paste the affected route(s) and sample trace IDs?
Priya (CS): routes: /v1/generate and /v1/chat (brightline-prod). Sample traces: trace-9a3, trace-9b1. Error rates are stable, it's tail latency.
Marco (eng-platform): Noted. This looks like a batching/queueing regression on the serving runtime after kernel swap. Could be sequence-length degradation for Brightline workload.
Jen (sre): Agree with Marco. Quick check: are these customers hitting the shared hosted pool or Dedicated?
Priya (CS): Brightline is on Hosted but pinned to model redwood-v2-small, region us-west.
Samir (eng-oncall): Ok. Short-term mitigation options: 1) route Brightline to a Dedicated warm pool if customer allows (fastest), 2) enable prefix KV caching for their common prompts, 3) rollback kernel change to previous variant. Which do we have bandwidth for now?
Liam (eng): I can prototype a rollout to a smaller canary dedicated pool (option 1) but need infra help to spin capacity and a config route. ETA ~90m for canary if infra is free.
Aaron (infra): I can provision a 2-GPU standby pool in us-west in ~25m if we prioritize. Need confirmation to proceed.
Samir (eng-oncall): @Aaron please provision standby pool. @Liam prepare routing rule. @Marco prepare a fallback policy that directs brightline-prod to dedicated pool for 1 hour, then evaluate.
Marco (eng-platform): Will open canary routing PR now. PR link: https://git.redwood/redwood/platform/merge_requests/1872 — includes roll-forward and metrics gating. Canary rollout plan in PR description.
Jen (sre): Also add a temporary p99 SLO slack alert override to avoid noisy ops alerts while we test. I’ll mute noisy alerts for brightline-prod telemetry.
Samir (eng-oncall): Parallel path: Marco, can you validate whether kernel swap rollback is safe? If canary fails, we might need immediate rollback.
Marco (eng-platform): I’ll run perf diff against the two kernels on a replay of brightline traces. Should have results in ~40m.
Priya (CS): Brightline CS: we told them ~2–3 hours for mitigation plan. I'll update them with the canary timeline and let them know you're provisioning.
Liam (eng): Routing PR ready for review, marking @Samir and @Marco as reviewers. If Aaron finishes infra, I’ll start canary in 30m.
Aaron (infra): Provision started. ETA 22m.
Maya (incident-bot): Incident created: INC-2026-4519 — Brightline tail latency. Severity: high. Incident channel: #inc-4519-brightline.
Samir (eng-oncall): Great. Owners: Samir (oncall triage), Marco (platform fallback & perf diff), Liam (routing canary), Aaron (infra provisioning), Jen (alerts). Next update in 30m or earlier with perf diff/canary start.
Priya (CS): Thank you all — CS will relay owners and SLA risk to Brightline and ask for permission to move to Dedicated if they accept.
Jen (sre): Quick note — if canary shows improvement, plan to keep traffic on dedicated for 1–4 hours and then evaluate rollback of kernel swap as a postmortem action.
Samir (eng-oncall): Closing loop: action items recorded in INC-2026-4519 and assigned in Jira ticket RJ-6123. Will post progress updates here. :thumbsup:
Priya (CS): Closing loop from CS side — I’ll post customer acknowledgment once they respond to the routing ask.
